chunks: Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Amir ibn 'Abdullah, who said:

I heard Abu 'Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There was upon the grave of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), a date-palm branch that shaded him from the sun, turning wherever the sun turned. So when the branch dried out, the grave became obscured, and its place was no longer known.'

key_terms.دَرَسَ: Became obscured or lost its distinctiveness
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)
key_terms.عَذْقٌ: A young date-palm or a branch of a date-palm tree
key_terms.قَبْرُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: The grave of Ibrahim (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What was the sign upon the grave of Ibrahim ibn al-Rasul (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the unique status of Ibrahim, the Prophet's firstborn, by describing a miraculous date-palm branch that shaded his grave and tracked the sun's movement. Its subsequent withering and the loss of the grave's precise location serve as a historical marker of his early death, a detail often discussed in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the Prophet's personal grief and the brevity of his son's life.

en.hubeali: Sahl, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Aamir Bin Abdullah who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There was upon the grave of Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> the son<sup>as</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> a tree which used to shade him<sup>as</sup> from the sun, circling wherever the sun circled. So when the tree dried out, the grave was obscured, so its place was no longer known’.
en.sarwar: 15. Sahl has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from ‘Amir ibn ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “

I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘On the gravesite of Ibrahim, son of the Messenger of Allah, there was a palm tree that provided shadow and it would turn as the sun moved to provide shadow for the site but when it dried up, the gravesite became old and indistinguishable.’”
